sentences.text: Gobisaurus was a herbivorous basal ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous.
The genus Gobisaurus is monotypic, containing only the single species Gobisaurus domoculus.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Gobisaurus domoculus at 6 meters and its weight at 3.5 tonnes.
The eye sockets of Gobisaurus domoculus were 20% of the skull length, and the external nostrils were 23% of the skull length.
Gobisaurus domoculus can be distinguished from its relative Shamosaurus scutatus by having a maxillary tooth row length of 26.6% of total skull length, compared to 40% in Shamosaurus.
A Sino-Soviet Expedition discovered the skeleton of Gobisaurus in the Gobi Desert of Inner Mongolia between 1959 and 1960.
Matthew K. Vickaryous, Anthony P. Russell, Philip John Currie, and Zhao Xijin named and described Gobisaurus domoculus in 2001.
The generic name Gobisaurus means "Gobi (Desert) lizard," referring to where the fossils were found.
Gobisaurus domoculus shares cranial similarities with Shamosaurus scutatus, including elliptical orbital fenestrae, large rounded external nares, and caudolaterally directed paroccipital processes.
Gobisaurus lived approximately 93 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
The fossil record for Gobisaurus spans from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
In 2014, Victoria Arbour concluded that Zhongyuansaurus might be a junior synonym of Gobisaurus based on the extensive postcranial remains found in its type specimen.
Victoria Arbour denied the distinction regarding cranial sculpting between Gobisaurus and Shamosaurus, concluding the degree of sculpting was approximately the same.
